Unravel the mesmerising beauty of Chhattisgarh
Chhattisgarh, located in central India, offers a captivating glimpse into ancient India through culture, art, religion, heritage of local and tribal communities and lush forests teeming with diverse flora and fauna - offering visitors an incredible glimpse of life from centuries past. As an emerging travel destination with untold potential. You'll discover gushing waterfalls, ancient temples and monuments steeped in history; lush forests full of species-rich fauna; vibrant culture echoing age-old traditions throughout this remarkable state.
Chhattisgarh boasts an amazing heritage sites that take you on an enthralling journey through time. Of these gems, Purani Basti stands out with its ancient fort dating back to 1460 AD surrounded by two tranquil ponds - Budha Talaab and Maharajband Talaab - that offer tranquil waters for relaxation. If you wish to delve even deeper into Chhattisgarh history, Mahant Ghasi Memorial Museum resides close by near Collectorate's Office; its walls conceal treasures that offer profound insight into Chhattisgarh heritage.
In the heart of Chhattisgarh's Bastar district, the scenic city of Jagdalpur is home to the Chitrakote waterfall, celebrated as the widest waterfall in India, earning the title of "Niagara of India" for its expansive beauty. You can extend your exploration by visiting the Kanger Valley National Park , a sanctuary of biodiversity bearing the prestigious title of an Asian Biosphere Reserve. Then you can go to visit Tirathgarh waterfall, a pristine cascade often referred to as 'The Milky Falls' due to its ethereal appearance, flows gracefully at an elevation of approximately 300 feet. Adding to Jagdalpur's allure is Dalpat Sagar, Chhattisgarh's largest artificial lake, dating back to 400 years. Originally it was constructed to harness rainwater, this historic reservoir invites you to its serene waters. If you find yourself in the bustling city centre of Raipur, the capital of Chhattisgarh, and crave a dose of nature's serenity, there are a couple of splendid options. Visit Gandhi Udyan Park and Swami Vivekanand Sarovar, both conveniently situated at the heart of the city. However, if you're in the mood for a road trip, visit Ghatarani Waterfalls which is just 85 kilometres away from Raipur.
Visit Kailash and Kutumsar Caves a subterranean wonder hidden 35 meters beneath the earth's surface. Stretching across a remarkable expanse of two kilometres, these caves hold the distinction of being the world's second-longest natural caves. A particularly awe-inspiring sight awaits you at the cave's end—a sacred Shivalinga. Another spiritual spot in Chhattisgarh is Danteshwari temple , revered as the divine embodiment of Shakti and a cherished deity of the Kakatiya rulers. Dating back to the 14th century, this temple showcases exquisite South Indian architectural influences. Furthermore, you can visit Bhoramdeo Temple, a spiritual attraction, drawing parallels to the iconic Sun Temple of Konark. Believed to have been constructed between the 7th and 12th centuries, this architectural marvel offers a glimpse into Chhattisgarh's rich spiritual heritage, explore the timeless echoes of devotion etched in stone. These spiritual wonders invite you to embark on a profound journey of exploration and reflection in the heart of Chhattisgarh.
Chhattisgarh showcases its distinct charm through its vast art and craft scene that embodies its deep traditions. Hand printing, an ancient craft made famous by Bastar's ail forest, brings natural vegetable dyes from these forest environments into play in this time-honored craft form of hand printing. This age-old technique can be seen adorning fabrics such as Bastar Kosa Sarees, dress materials and drapes. Additionally, cotton fabric craftmanship has long been recognized as an esteemed handicraft skill handed down from generation to generation. Tribes descended from Kabir the 14th-century weaver-poet are still weaving and hand printing fabrics using Kosa thread to produce beautifully intricate textiles, while bamboo art continues to thrive throughout Chhattisgarh, often by tribal artisans demonstrating their masterful craftwork. Bastar and Raigarh districts have gained notoriety for their bell metal handicrafts - an amalgamation of brass and bronze. Godna, an artistic movement pioneered in Jangala, Chhattisgarh by women from Godna, is also noted. These women adorn textiles with traditional tattoo motifs to add another unique component to Chhattisgarh crafts. Also noteworthy are Loha Shilp's dark and raw metal artifacts and figurines made out of Loha Shilp's artistic expertise to round out Chhattisgarh crafts' diverse repertoire.
Chhattisgarh's culinary landscape is deeply rooted in its production of staple crops like rice, bajra, and jawar. Food culture thrives here with an exquisite range of flavours and dishes that capture the spirit of the region - start your day right by trying a delicious Muthia for breakfast! Aamat is a delicacy from Bastar that often rivals Sambhar in popularity. Chila, similar to flat chapatis and made with rice batter infused with Urad Dal is another local specialty; Faraa are delicious Indian momos reminiscent of Chinese momos. Furthermore, Tilgur holds a special place among locals during special events and festivals like Makar Sankranti when people prepare and share it together; making this part of Chhattisgarh's culinary history.
Chhattisgarh celebrates several vibrant festivals, offering a captivating glimpse into state's culture. The Hareli festival, a celebration, that derives its name from 'Haryali,' meaning greenery in Hindi and unites farming communities in a jubilant display of gratitude for the bountiful harvest. Another significant festival is Pat Jatra, an annual event coinciding with Hareli amavasya. This marks the commencement of the Bastar Dusshera Festival, a famed 75-day extravaganza that pays homage to Goddess Danteswari. Pat Jatra revolves around the veneration of Sal tree wood, known locally as 'Thurlu Kotla' or 'Tika pata.' This ritual is a cherished tradition, deeply rooted in the cultural heritage of the Bastar region.

One of Chhattisgarh's hidden gems is the Kanker Palace , now a part of India's cherished heritage hotels. Originally named Radha Niwas Bagicha, this architectural marvel traces its roots to the early 20th century.
Chhattisgarh is home to Indira Kala Sangeet Vishwavidyalaya , India’s first university dedicated to music, dance, theatre, and fine arts.
Chhattisgarh is the birthplace of the founder of Vallabh sect, Saint Vallabhacharya .
In 2009, Achanakmar Tiger Reserve in Chhattisgarh received the prestigious designation of a Project Tiger reserve. This lush expanse, particularly in the Bilaspur district, spanning an impressive 557 square kilometres, shelters a remarkable population of tigers, making it a haven for wildlife enthusiasts.
The Temple of Bhoramdeo is often referred to as the "Khajuraho of Chhattisgarh," owing to its intricate and exotic sculptures.
